pairs.subject: metric-gates
pairs.evidence: lib/foundry/mesh/gates/mesh-score.ts:57 The context grades each vendor-generated mesh at runtime against fixed authored ceilings and the budget the caller requested, never against an earlier recorded reading of a codebase metric, so the subject's precondition (a 'how much' gate compared to a committed baseline or prior artifact) does not hold; a search of lib/foundry/mesh/ for ratchet, snapshot, benchmark and elapsed found no hits.

techniques.evidence: lib/foundry/mesh/gates/mesh-score.ts:57 Absolute per-mesh thresholds, not a committed baseline gated on direction; nothing here is a legacy count being driven down.
lib/foundry/mesh/gates/polycount.ts:58 Budgets are authored per asset class, not a regression snapshot of totals, so there is no count-only baseline to worry about substitution in.

lib/foundry/mesh/gates/face-budget.ts:123 The gate compares a deterministic triangle count of a delivered artifact; it is not a timing gate on code, so there is no cost standard to restate as a source-text operation.
lib/foundry/mesh/gates/face-budget.ts:42 No noisy instrument is swapped for a work count here; the 10% band covers decimator landing error on an asset, not a counter's repeat variance in a CI lane.

lib/foundry/mesh/gates/mesh-score.ts:231 There is no published coverage or parity metric whose population can be moved toward it; the closest analogue (the geometry-only scorer listing in GATE_ONLY_CODES what it cannot see, and face-budget returning 'unmeasured' instead of passing) matches the technique's honesty rules in spirit, but it is a tier split inside a per-asset grader.

pairs.registryProposal: Per-asset acceptance graders for generated media (polycount and budget-honoured checks, unmeasured-not-pass) keep landing next to metric-gates in the lexical map. Their governing subject is generated-output-grading (media-generation). metric-gates could say in its scope section that a threshold on a generated artifact's measured property is not a metric gate unless it is compared against a recorded earlier reading.
